Subject: POC Performance roadmap, gates & owner commitments

Hi Samira — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps to get the POC scheduled. I want this to be lightweight and focused on measurable outcomes so your engineers can evaluate impact quickly.

High-level objective:
- Validate Redwood inference latency and cost for FjordTech’s product search reranking workload (75M monthly queries).

Success criteria (proposed):
1) Latency: 95th percentile under 220ms for 512-token rerank requests during steady-state load.
2) Quality: top-5 rerank accuracy lift >= 6% against your baseline metric (as measured by A/B on the test corpus attached).
3) Cost: per-10k-request token cost < target provided in procurement (we can iterate).

Proposed milestone timeline (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (Kickoff, 1 hour): Confirm access, goals, and data samples (owners: Rachel / FjordTech eng lead Jose).
- Week 1 (Baseline run): Redwood executes baseline model runs + preliminary latency profile (owner: Marcus).
- Week 2 (Optimization sprint): Batching and caching configuration; quantization recommendation applied; run with load generator (owner: Marissa).
- Week 3 (Readout & acceptance): Joint readout, sample comparison, decision gate (accept / extend / iterate).

Check-ins: 30-min sync every Tuesday (standup-focused) + one 60-min mid-sprint demo at end of Week 2.

Attachments: fjord-tech-eval-plan.xlsx (POC plan & data checklist), poe-success-metrics.csv (sample labels).

Open items for Samira / FjordTech:
- Confirm preferred kickoff window (Oct 26–29) and primary engineering contact (Jose or alternate).
- Provide sample request/response logs (anonymized) or a representative subset for model evaluation.
- Procurement contact for any MSA/PO needs so we can share the SLA draft.

If this looks good I’ll send a calendar invite for Kickoff + include Marcus and Marissa as leads for the baseline and optimization runs.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim

Hi all — following up with the load-generator template and a few tuning suggestions based on your expected query distribution. I’ve attached a short YAML and included example k6 and locust snippets in the Drive folder.

Tuning suggestions (short):
- Start with 50 concurrent virtual users for the first baseline run to validate cold-start and batching behavior.
- Increase to 200 concurrent for the steady-state profile; observe 95p latency and token throughput.
- Use the provided script to simulate variable sequence lengths — this helps avoid optimistic latency estimates.

Samira / Jose: once you confirm you’ve placed samples in the shared Drive I’ll coordinate Marcus to run the baseline on Fri Oct 30; otherwise we can push the baseline into Week 1 of November.

Action: Jose to share drive link to anonymized samples by EOD Thu Oct 29.

Thanks,
